block, labs false.description:
Build a Doc, a report, plan or write-up longer than a screen, in a block beside your pane that the user (and anyone the session is shared with) watches fill in. Make the outline first with new, so they see every section at once; then fill each section in order and say one sentence about it in the pane. Docs are kept: to go on with an earlier one, doc list and then doc open. Never write the Doc's files by hand.
- new {sections, title, beside?}: A Doc: a block beside your pane that holds a report, plan or write-up, with its outline (every section's heading and intent) shown at once. Returns the block and the section ids (s1, s2, …); fill them next, in order.
- list: The Docs kept on this machine, newest first: id, title, made, updated, who made it, the block that shows it now (open) and whether it is shared. Any Doc an earlier session wrote is here, open or not; doc open shows one in a block, which you can then fill.
- open {doc, beside?}: Open a Doc from doc list in a block beside your pane, to read or to go on with: returns the block, and you can doc fill it, as after doc new (the sections are the outline's, s1, s2, …; its state has them). A Doc already open in a block is that block, not a second one: the user may have it open beside another pane.
- fill {block, markdown, section}: Write one section of a Doc (its block, the section id, its Markdown): headings, paragraphs, lists, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, links and tables. No HTML. A picture is ![alt](assets/<name>) after doc asset has put it there. A section is at most 64 KB, a Doc 40 sections and 1 MiB; filling a section again replaces it.

A callout is a quote whose first line is [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION], as on GitHub: "> [!TIP]" then "> Run it twice." Keep them for what the reader mustn't miss.

Three kinds of fenced block draw as more than code, in the section that talks about them.
Stat tiles: a ```stats fence holding a list of 1 to 6 tiles; label and value are text, delta and its tone (up, down or flat) are optional. For example:
```stats
[{"label": "Sessions", "value": "1,284", "delta": "+12%", "tone": "up"}, {"label": "Errors", "value": "3"}]
```
A chart: a ```chart fence holding a JSON spec. type is "bar" or "line"; title is optional; x is the key of each row that labels it; y is a key, or a list of up to 4 keys, whose values are numbers (not strings); rows is 1 to 200 objects. A line chart's x must go up: numbers, ISO dates (2026-01-31), or labels listed in order with "order": [...]. For example:
```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "Sales by month", "x": "month", "y": ["sales"], "rows": [{"month": "Jan", "sales": 12}, {"month": "Feb", "sales": 19}]}
```
A drawing: a ```svg fence holding one <svg> element, with xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" on it and a viewBox. Any text after svg on the fence line is its alt text. It is shown as a picture, so scripts in it don't run.
Colours are named, so a Doc reads in light and dark: leaf, pepper, sky, plum, sun, stone, ink (text) and paper (the page), each with a soft fill (leaf-soft, stone-soft, …). In a drawing, fill, stroke, stop-color and color take a name; a chart's optional "colors" names one of the six hues for each y series ("colors": ["leaf", "stone"]).
Grey first (stone and ink), one accent per figure. Text stays ink. For example:
```svg Idea to app
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 160 40" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle"><rect x="2" y="8" width="60" height="24" rx="4" fill="stone-soft" stroke="stone"/><text x="32" y="24" fill="ink">Idea</text><path d="M62 20 H98" stroke="ink"/><rect x="98" y="8" width="60" height="24" rx="4" fill="leaf-soft" stroke="leaf"/><text x="128" y="24" fill="ink">App</text></svg>
```
Every fence is checked before anything is written: a bad chart, tile or drawing is refused with one line saying what to fix, and the section stays as it was.
- asset {block, name, data?, path?}: Put a picture in a Doc (its block, a name, and one of path or data): a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 2 MB, at most 20 per Doc. path is an absolute path to a file you saved; an agent on a machine of its own sends data (base64) instead. What the bytes are decides the type, so the name has to end in the right extension (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp); an SVG file is refused: draw it with a ```svg fence. Returns assets/<name>; show it in a section with ![what it shows](assets/<name>). Put the asset before the doc fill that names it: a fill naming an asset the Doc doesn't have is refused. Only assets/ images show; an http:// or ../ one is refused. A name already used is replaced. For example: {"kind": "asset", "block": 7, "name": "flow.png", "path": "/tmp/flow.png"}.
- share {block}: Ask the user to share a finished Doc (its block) with a link anyone can open, without an account. A card asks them on the Doc and nothing is published until they tap Share; this returns {status: "waiting"} at once. Call share again on the same block to learn the outcome: shared (with the url, which you can give the user), declined, lapsed (a card nobody answered in a day) or failed (with why). A Doc already shared answers shared. Asking again after a decline raises a new card. Don't ask more than once for a Doc unless the user wants it.

block, labs true.description:
Build a Doc, a report, plan or write-up longer than a screen, in a block beside your pane that the user (and anyone the session is shared with) watches fill in. Make the outline first with new, so they see every section at once; then fill each section in order and say one sentence about it in the pane. Docs are kept: to go on with an earlier one, doc list and then doc open. Never write the Doc's files by hand.
- new {sections, title, beside?}: A Doc: a block beside your pane that holds a report, plan or write-up, with its outline (every section's heading and intent) shown at once. Returns the block and the section ids (s1, s2, …); fill them next, in order.
- list: The Docs kept on this machine, newest first: id, title, made, updated, who made it, the block that shows it now (open) and whether it is shared. Any Doc an earlier session wrote is here, open or not; doc open shows one in a block, which you can then fill.
- open {doc, beside?}: Open a Doc from doc list in a block beside your pane, to read or to go on with: returns the block, and you can doc fill it, as after doc new (the sections are the outline's, s1, s2, …; its state has them). A Doc already open in a block is that block, not a second one: the user may have it open beside another pane.
- fill {block, markdown, section}: Write one section of a Doc (its block, the section id, its Markdown): headings, paragraphs, lists, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, links and tables. No HTML. A picture is ![alt](assets/<name>) after doc asset has put it there. A section is at most 64 KB, a Doc 40 sections and 1 MiB; filling a section again replaces it.

A callout is a quote whose first line is [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION], as on GitHub: "> [!TIP]" then "> Run it twice." Keep them for what the reader mustn't miss.

Three kinds of fenced block draw as more than code, in the section that talks about them.
Stat tiles: a ```stats fence holding a list of 1 to 6 tiles; label and value are text, delta and its tone (up, down or flat) are optional. For example:
```stats
[{"label": "Sessions", "value": "1,284", "delta": "+12%", "tone": "up"}, {"label": "Errors", "value": "3"}]
```
A chart: a ```chart fence holding a JSON spec. type is "bar" or "line"; title is optional; x is the key of each row that labels it; y is a key, or a list of up to 4 keys, whose values are numbers (not strings); rows is 1 to 200 objects. A line chart's x must go up: numbers, ISO dates (2026-01-31), or labels listed in order with "order": [...]. For example:
```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "Sales by month", "x": "month", "y": ["sales"], "rows": [{"month": "Jan", "sales": 12}, {"month": "Feb", "sales": 19}]}
```
A drawing: a ```svg fence holding one <svg> element, with xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" on it and a viewBox. Any text after svg on the fence line is its alt text. It is shown as a picture, so scripts in it don't run.
Colours are named, so a Doc reads in light and dark: leaf, pepper, sky, plum, sun, stone, ink (text) and paper (the page), each with a soft fill (leaf-soft, stone-soft, …). In a drawing, fill, stroke, stop-color and color take a name; a chart's optional "colors" names one of the six hues for each y series ("colors": ["leaf", "stone"]).
Grey first (stone and ink), one accent per figure. Text stays ink. For example:
```svg Idea to app
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 160 40" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle"><rect x="2" y="8" width="60" height="24" rx="4" fill="stone-soft" stroke="stone"/><text x="32" y="24" fill="ink">Idea</text><path d="M62 20 H98" stroke="ink"/><rect x="98" y="8" width="60" height="24" rx="4" fill="leaf-soft" stroke="leaf"/><text x="128" y="24" fill="ink">App</text></svg>
```
Every fence is checked before anything is written: a bad chart, tile or drawing is refused with one line saying what to fix, and the section stays as it was.
- asset {block, name, data?, path?}: Put a picture in a Doc (its block, a name, and one of path or data): a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 2 MB, at most 20 per Doc. path is an absolute path to a file you saved; an agent on a machine of its own sends data (base64) instead. What the bytes are decides the type, so the name has to end in the right extension (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp); an SVG file is refused: draw it with a ```svg fence. Returns assets/<name>; show it in a section with ![what it shows](assets/<name>). Put the asset before the doc fill that names it: a fill naming an asset the Doc doesn't have is refused. Only assets/ images show; an http:// or ../ one is refused. A name already used is replaced. For example: {"kind": "asset", "block": 7, "name": "flow.png", "path": "/tmp/flow.png"}.
- share {block}: Ask the user to share a finished Doc (its block) with a link anyone can open, without an account. A card asks them on the Doc and nothing is published until they tap Share; this returns {status: "waiting"} at once. Call share again on the same block to learn the outcome: shared (with the url, which you can give the user), declined, lapsed (a card nobody answered in a day) or failed (with why). A Doc already shared answers shared. Asking again after a decline raises a new card. Don't ask more than once for a Doc unless the user wants it.

block, labs true.description:
Write to a project's board in Arugula control, at once: what you write lands now, labelled as your person's agent on this machine, never as them. Their boards.write grant over the project says you may, never more than their role. A board is rows, one piece of work each, and its lanes (Next, Doing, Review, Done) follow the live state of the work: you can't set a lane or a status; the platform refuses those, "lanes follow the work". To get a person's decision, ask them: the ask kind puts a question on a row (who, the question, why, up to four options, a recommendation); they answer on the board, and you read the answer in board_read (the row's asked, newest first), never by waiting on it. What you can set is the plan: groups, the board's named, ordered sections (phases, waves, areas), and the group each row is in. You may make a board (an epic, with a goal), set its title and goal, close it with a note saying what a person can now do, and open it again; make, rename, move and delete groups (add_zone, edit_zone, move_zone, delete_zone), and put a row in a group or out of one (add_row with zone, move); add a row for an issue or a PR (a PR that names the issue of a row is attached to that row, and an item already on the board isn't added again; the answer says so), set a row's note, attach work (a PR, an agent block or a run, which moves the lane) or proof (a run or a link, which marks a Done row proven) to a row, take off an attachment you made, and remove or repoint a row you added. You may not remove or repoint a row someone else added, or delete a group that holds one. A note, a pointer or a group's title names the rev board_read showed for it; if it has changed since, this says so: board_read again and retry. Every kind returns the board as it is now.
- add_row {board, note?, pointer?, zone?}: Add a row last (in a group, if you name one): an issue or a PR as its item (or a note), with a one-line note. A PR that names the issue of a row is attached to that row; an item already on the board isn't added again.
- set {board, row, note?, pointer?, rev?, status?}: Set a row's note or pointer (with its rev), or clear an old status.
- move {board, row, before?, rev?, zone?}: Move a row to a group (zone), or out of its group (zone: null), and set its place in it. A lane is never set.
- attach {board, pointer, role, row}: Attach work (a PR, an agent block or a run) or proof (a run or a link) to a row.
- detach {attachment, board}: Take off an attachment you made.
- ask {board, question, row, who, options?, recommend?, why?}: Ask a person of the project a question on a row (an issue or a PR; one open ask per row), with up to four options or none for free text. They answer on the board, and the answer is the row's asked in board_read: read it there. You can't answer an ask.
- remove_row {board, row}: Remove a row you added.
- create_board {title, goal?, project?}: Make a board in a project, with a goal (an epic); returns it.
- edit_board {board, goal?, title?}: Set a board's title and/or goal.
- close_board {board, done_note}: Close a board with a note saying what a person can now do.
- reopen_board {board}: Open a closed board again, keeping its note.
- add_zone {board, title}: Add a group to a board, last: a named section (a phase, a wave, an area) that rows go in.
- edit_zone {board, rev, title, zone}: Rename a group (with its rev).
- move_zone {board, zone, before?}: Move a group among a board's groups.
- delete_zone {board, zone}: Delete a group that is empty or holds only rows you added, with its rows.

full, labs false.description:
Build a Doc, a report, plan or write-up longer than a screen, in a block beside your pane that the user (and anyone the session is shared with) watches fill in. Make the outline first with new, so they see every section at once; then fill each section in order and say one sentence about it in the pane. Docs are kept: to go on with an earlier one, doc list and then doc open. Never write the Doc's files by hand.
- new {sections, title, beside?}: A Doc: a block beside your pane that holds a report, plan or write-up, with its outline (every section's heading and intent) shown at once. Returns the block and the section ids (s1, s2, …); fill them next, in order.
- list: The Docs kept on this machine, newest first: id, title, made, updated, who made it, the block that shows it now (open) and whether it is shared. Any Doc an earlier session wrote is here, open or not; doc open shows one in a block, which you can then fill.
- open {doc, beside?}: Open a Doc from doc list in a block beside your pane, to read or to go on with: returns the block, and you can doc fill it, as after doc new (the sections are the outline's, s1, s2, …; its state has them). A Doc already open in a block is that block, not a second one: the user may have it open beside another pane.
- fill {block, markdown, section}: Write one section of a Doc (its block, the section id, its Markdown): headings, paragraphs, lists, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, links and tables. No HTML. A picture is ![alt](assets/<name>) after doc asset has put it there. A section is at most 64 KB, a Doc 40 sections and 1 MiB; filling a section again replaces it.

A callout is a quote whose first line is [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION], as on GitHub: "> [!TIP]" then "> Run it twice." Keep them for what the reader mustn't miss.

Three kinds of fenced block draw as more than code, in the section that talks about them.
Stat tiles: a ```stats fence holding a list of 1 to 6 tiles; label and value are text, delta and its tone (up, down or flat) are optional. For example:
```stats
[{"label": "Sessions", "value": "1,284", "delta": "+12%", "tone": "up"}, {"label": "Errors", "value": "3"}]
```
A chart: a ```chart fence holding a JSON spec. type is "bar" or "line"; title is optional; x is the key of each row that labels it; y is a key, or a list of up to 4 keys, whose values are numbers (not strings); rows is 1 to 200 objects. A line chart's x must go up: numbers, ISO dates (2026-01-31), or labels listed in order with "order": [...]. For example:
```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "Sales by month", "x": "month", "y": ["sales"], "rows": [{"month": "Jan", "sales": 12}, {"month": "Feb", "sales": 19}]}
```
A drawing: a ```svg fence holding one <svg> element, with xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" on it and a viewBox. Any text after svg on the fence line is its alt text. It is shown as a picture, so scripts in it don't run.
Colours are named, so a Doc reads in light and dark: leaf, pepper, sky, plum, sun, stone, ink (text) and paper (the page), each with a soft fill (leaf-soft, stone-soft, …). In a drawing, fill, stroke, stop-color and color take a name; a chart's optional "colors" names one of the six hues for each y series ("colors": ["leaf", "stone"]).
Grey first (stone and ink), one accent per figure. Text stays ink. For example:
```svg Idea to app
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 160 40" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle"><rect x="2" y="8" width="60" height="24" rx="4" fill="stone-soft" stroke="stone"/><text x="32" y="24" fill="ink">Idea</text><path d="M62 20 H98" stroke="ink"/><rect x="98" y="8" width="60" height="24" rx="4" fill="leaf-soft" stroke="leaf"/><text x="128" y="24" fill="ink">App</text></svg>
```
Every fence is checked before anything is written: a bad chart, tile or drawing is refused with one line saying what to fix, and the section stays as it was.
- asset {block, name, data?, path?}: Put a picture in a Doc (its block, a name, and one of path or data): a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 2 MB, at most 20 per Doc. path is an absolute path to a file you saved; an agent on a machine of its own sends data (base64) instead. What the bytes are decides the type, so the name has to end in the right extension (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp); an SVG file is refused: draw it with a ```svg fence. Returns assets/<name>; show it in a section with ![what it shows](assets/<name>). Put the asset before the doc fill that names it: a fill naming an asset the Doc doesn't have is refused. Only assets/ images show; an http:// or ../ one is refused. A name already used is replaced. For example: {"kind": "asset", "block": 7, "name": "flow.png", "path": "/tmp/flow.png"}.
- share {block}: Ask the user to share a finished Doc (its block) with a link anyone can open, without an account. A card asks them on the Doc and nothing is published until they tap Share; this returns {status: "waiting"} at once. Call share again on the same block to learn the outcome: shared (with the url, which you can give the user), declined, lapsed (a card nobody answered in a day) or failed (with why). A Doc already shared answers shared. Asking again after a decline raises a new card. Don't ask more than once for a Doc unless the user wants it.

full, labs true.description:
A task for an agent offered on this machine or another (your own, your team's, a teammate's), over A2A: send it, follow it, answer its questions, or cancel it.
- send {agent, dir?, machine?, pr?, task?, text?, wait?}: Hand a task to an agent offered on this machine or another (list kind agents lists them; machine can be left out): text is what to do, in that agent's project there, with what it needs to know (it doesn't see your conversation). Its owner may first have to allow it. Waits for it to finish (or ask you something) and returns its reply and the patch's stat; the patch itself is kept here. With pr: true it opens a pull request in its own project instead, and the reply links it.
- get {agent, dir?, machine?, pr?, task?, text?, wait?}: A task's state now (with wait: once it finishes or asks): its status, reply and patch's stat.
- answer {agent, dir?, machine?, pr?, task?, text?, wait?}: Answer the question a task asked (its state says input_required), or send a finished task a follow-up: text, then wait as send does.
- cancel {agent, dir?, machine?, pr?, task?, text?, wait?}: Stop a task you sent.
- review {agent, dir?, machine?, pr?, task?, text?, wait?}: A finished task's patch, applied to a scratch copy of your checkout and shown in a diff block beside you, for the user to look at before anything changes here. Says whether it applies cleanly.
- apply {agent, dir?, machine?, pr?, task?, text?, wait?}: Apply a finished task's patch in your checkout (git apply --3way): which files changed, conflicts to resolve, hunks that didn't apply, and new binary files the task left out.

full, labs true.description:
Build a Doc, a report, plan or write-up longer than a screen, in a block beside your pane that the user (and anyone the session is shared with) watches fill in. Make the outline first with new, so they see every section at once; then fill each section in order and say one sentence about it in the pane. Docs are kept: to go on with an earlier one, doc list and then doc open. Never write the Doc's files by hand.
- new {sections, title, beside?}: A Doc: a block beside your pane that holds a report, plan or write-up, with its outline (every section's heading and intent) shown at once. Returns the block and the section ids (s1, s2, …); fill them next, in order.
- list: The Docs kept on this machine, newest first: id, title, made, updated, who made it, the block that shows it now (open) and whether it is shared. Any Doc an earlier session wrote is here, open or not; doc open shows one in a block, which you can then fill.
- open {doc, beside?}: Open a Doc from doc list in a block beside your pane, to read or to go on with: returns the block, and you can doc fill it, as after doc new (the sections are the outline's, s1, s2, …; its state has them). A Doc already open in a block is that block, not a second one: the user may have it open beside another pane.
- fill {block, markdown, section}: Write one section of a Doc (its block, the section id, its Markdown): headings, paragraphs, lists, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, links and tables. No HTML. A picture is ![alt](assets/<name>) after doc asset has put it there. A section is at most 64 KB, a Doc 40 sections and 1 MiB; filling a section again replaces it.

A callout is a quote whose first line is [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION], as on GitHub: "> [!TIP]" then "> Run it twice." Keep them for what the reader mustn't miss.

Three kinds of fenced block draw as more than code, in the section that talks about them.
Stat tiles: a ```stats fence holding a list of 1 to 6 tiles; label and value are text, delta and its tone (up, down or flat) are optional. For example:
```stats
[{"label": "Sessions", "value": "1,284", "delta": "+12%", "tone": "up"}, {"label": "Errors", "value": "3"}]
```
A chart: a ```chart fence holding a JSON spec. type is "bar" or "line"; title is optional; x is the key of each row that labels it; y is a key, or a list of up to 4 keys, whose values are numbers (not strings); rows is 1 to 200 objects. A line chart's x must go up: numbers, ISO dates (2026-01-31), or labels listed in order with "order": [...]. For example:
```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "Sales by month", "x": "month", "y": ["sales"], "rows": [{"month": "Jan", "sales": 12}, {"month": "Feb", "sales": 19}]}
```
A drawing: a ```svg fence holding one <svg> element, with xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" on it and a viewBox. Any text after svg on the fence line is its alt text. It is shown as a picture, so scripts in it don't run.
Colours are named, so a Doc reads in light and dark: leaf, pepper, sky, plum, sun, stone, ink (text) and paper (the page), each with a soft fill (leaf-soft, stone-soft, …). In a drawing, fill, stroke, stop-color and color take a name; a chart's optional "colors" names one of the six hues for each y series ("colors": ["leaf", "stone"]).
Grey first (stone and ink), one accent per figure. Text stays ink. For example:
```svg Idea to app
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 160 40" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle"><rect x="2" y="8" width="60" height="24" rx="4" fill="stone-soft" stroke="stone"/><text x="32" y="24" fill="ink">Idea</text><path d="M62 20 H98" stroke="ink"/><rect x="98" y="8" width="60" height="24" rx="4" fill="leaf-soft" stroke="leaf"/><text x="128" y="24" fill="ink">App</text></svg>
```
Every fence is checked before anything is written: a bad chart, tile or drawing is refused with one line saying what to fix, and the section stays as it was.
- asset {block, name, data?, path?}: Put a picture in a Doc (its block, a name, and one of path or data): a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 2 MB, at most 20 per Doc. path is an absolute path to a file you saved; an agent on a machine of its own sends data (base64) instead. What the bytes are decides the type, so the name has to end in the right extension (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp); an SVG file is refused: draw it with a ```svg fence. Returns assets/<name>; show it in a section with ![what it shows](assets/<name>). Put the asset before the doc fill that names it: a fill naming an asset the Doc doesn't have is refused. Only assets/ images show; an http:// or ../ one is refused. A name already used is replaced. For example: {"kind": "asset", "block": 7, "name": "flow.png", "path": "/tmp/flow.png"}.
- share {block}: Ask the user to share a finished Doc (its block) with a link anyone can open, without an account. A card asks them on the Doc and nothing is published until they tap Share; this returns {status: "waiting"} at once. Call share again on the same block to learn the outcome: shared (with the url, which you can give the user), declined, lapsed (a card nobody answered in a day) or failed (with why). A Doc already shared answers shared. Asking again after a decline raises a new card. Don't ask more than once for a Doc unless the user wants it.

full, labs true.description:
Write to a project's board in Arugula control, at once: what you write lands now, labelled as your person's agent on this machine, never as them. Their boards.write grant over the project says you may, never more than their role. A board is rows, one piece of work each, and its lanes (Next, Doing, Review, Done) follow the live state of the work: you can't set a lane or a status; the platform refuses those, "lanes follow the work". To get a person's decision, ask them: the ask kind puts a question on a row (who, the question, why, up to four options, a recommendation); they answer on the board, and you read the answer in board_read (the row's asked, newest first), never by waiting on it. What you can set is the plan: groups, the board's named, ordered sections (phases, waves, areas), and the group each row is in. You may make a board (an epic, with a goal), set its title and goal, close it with a note saying what a person can now do, and open it again; make, rename, move and delete groups (add_zone, edit_zone, move_zone, delete_zone), and put a row in a group or out of one (add_row with zone, move); add a row for an issue or a PR (a PR that names the issue of a row is attached to that row, and an item already on the board isn't added again; the answer says so), set a row's note, attach work (a PR, an agent block or a run, which moves the lane) or proof (a run or a link, which marks a Done row proven) to a row, take off an attachment you made, and remove or repoint a row you added. You may not remove or repoint a row someone else added, or delete a group that holds one. A note, a pointer or a group's title names the rev board_read showed for it; if it has changed since, this says so: board_read again and retry. Every kind returns the board as it is now.
- add_row {board, note?, pointer?, zone?}: Add a row last (in a group, if you name one): an issue or a PR as its item (or a note), with a one-line note. A PR that names the issue of a row is attached to that row; an item already on the board isn't added again.
- set {board, row, note?, pointer?, rev?, status?}: Set a row's note or pointer (with its rev), or clear an old status.
- move {board, row, before?, rev?, zone?}: Move a row to a group (zone), or out of its group (zone: null), and set its place in it. A lane is never set.
- attach {board, pointer, role, row}: Attach work (a PR, an agent block or a run) or proof (a run or a link) to a row.
- detach {attachment, board}: Take off an attachment you made.
- ask {board, question, row, who, options?, recommend?, why?}: Ask a person of the project a question on a row (an issue or a PR; one open ask per row), with up to four options or none for free text. They answer on the board, and the answer is the row's asked in board_read: read it there. You can't answer an ask.
- remove_row {board, row}: Remove a row you added.
- create_board {title, goal?, project?}: Make a board in a project, with a goal (an epic); returns it.
- edit_board {board, goal?, title?}: Set a board's title and/or goal.
- close_board {board, done_note}: Close a board with a note saying what a person can now do.
- reopen_board {board}: Open a closed board again, keeping its note.
- add_zone {board, title}: Add a group to a board, last: a named section (a phase, a wave, an area) that rows go in.
- edit_zone {board, rev, title, zone}: Rename a group (with its rev).
- move_zone {board, zone, before?}: Move a group among a board's groups.
- delete_zone {board, zone}: Delete a group that is empty or holds only rows you added, with its rows.

Your person's trackers.write grant over the project says you may, never more than their role. A write may wait: when the connection is set to approve each agent write (the default) it is kept for a person to approve, edit or drop in the project's Triage, and this says "waiting for a person to approve it" with its id; nothing has reached Plane yet, and you can't approve it yourself. When the connection allows agent writes it lands at once. What is sent ends with a line saying it was sent via Arugula by your person's agent on this machine. Items are named by their fi_ id (forge_read lists them) or IDENT-N, like ARUGU-7. Assignees are not supported.

- comment {item, text, project?}: Comment on a work item (may wait for a person).
- close {as, item, project?}: Close a work item as completed or cancelled (may wait for a person).
- reopen {item, project?}: Open a closed work item again (may wait for a person).
- edit {item, body?, project?, title?}: Change a work item's title or body (may wait for a person).

What's here to work with, by kind (default panes).
- panes (the default): Every pane and block (terminals, browsers, agents): where it is, what it runs, whether it needs attention, who started it.
- conversations {all?, cwd?, limit?, live?, query?}: Claude Code conversations on this machine, from a terminal or the desktop app's Code tab, newest first: id, title, folder, first and last prompt, where it's open now, and the agent block that has it. show kind conversation opens one.

- agents {fresh?, query?}: The agents the user's team offers: every Claude Code agent recipe offered on this machine, the user's other machines, their teams' and teammates', one line each: name, machine and owner, model, description. A machine that's offline shows its agents as last seen. To hand one a task (this machine's too), delegate {kind: send, agent: NAME}; for a fix in its own project, with pr: true. To run one of this machine's beside you, start_agent {recipe: NAME}.
- cloud_workspaces: The Cloud workspaces of the user's projects in Arugula control (machines in the cloud with their repositories checked out, each with tabs of agents): each one's id, name, project, state (starting, running, paused, failed) and machine. - cloud_tabs {cloud_workspace}: A Cloud workspace's tabs: the agent blocks on its machine, by pane number, with their status.
- linked_repos {project?}: The GitHub repos linked to one of the user's projects in Arugula control (default their personal one): each one's name, whether it's private, and, for one unlinked, when its rows are purged.
- threads: The conversations agents here may read or post in, through grants this machine's owner gave in Arugula control: team channels, their DMs, and the threads on issues and PRs. Narrow it with label (its issue's), tracker (an issue's number: the issues its body names as #N, and those naming it), asker (an account, or me), mine (only those this machine's agents started) and going.
